claim: With AWS CLI version 2 integration, developers sign in to the AWS CLI with the same IAM Identity Center or Active Directory credentials they use for IAM Identity Center, can list and switch between assigned accounts and roles, and the CLI manages short-term credentials automatically.
question: How do developers use the AWS CLI with IAM Identity Center without long-term access keys?

values.display: the same Active Directory or IAM Identity Center credentials
list and switch between accounts and roles
The CLI manages short-term credentials automatically

qualifiers.scope: AWS CLI version 2 with IAM Identity Center

evidence.quote: AWS Command Line Interface (CLI) version 2 integration with IAM Identity Center simplifies the sign-in process.

Developers can sign in directly to the AWS CLI using the same Active Directory or IAM Identity Center credentials that they normally use to sign in to IAM Identity Center, and access their assigned accounts and roles.
Developers can list and switch between accounts and roles to which they have assigned access.
The CLI manages short-term credentials automatically so developers can start in and stay in the CLI securely without interruption, and run long running scripts.
